An asteroid belt of countless drifting rocks recedes into the dark behind the rig, each a faint tumbling silhouette against the stars.
A vast banded gas giant looms huge behind the mined asteroid, its stormy light washing cold color across the worksite.
A harsh small sun hangs distant and white, casting long hard-edged shadows across the scarred rock and machinery.
A distant refinery fleet glows amber and gold against the black, its cluster of lights a small city in the void.
A cold blue starfield stretches in every direction, ancient and indifferent, the rig a mote of metal lost within it.
A haze of dust and pulverized debris drifts through the worksite, catching the sun in thin veils of pale amber light.
Other mining rigs show as faint moving lights across the belt, their running lamps blinking slow in the far dark.
A ringed planet hangs beyond the asteroid field, its great disc tilted, rings catching sunlight in a bright diagonal arc.
A cluster of tumbling rocks spins slowly together nearby, their irregular shapes casting shifting shadows across one another.
The deep black of open space frames everything, absolute and crushing, the stars cold and unreachable in every direction.
A long debris field trails away from a shattered asteroid, a loose river of fragments glinting in the weak sunlight.
Two moons hang close together beyond the belt, one large and cratered, one small and grey, both utterly lifeless.
A transport freighter crawls through the middle distance, its running lights strobing, hull scarred and bulky with ore containers.
The sun catches the face of a slow-rotating boulder, the lit half brilliant white, the shadow half absolute and black.
A dense patch of belt debris crowds the sky overhead, hundreds of rocks layered deep, blocking stars behind their mass.
A processing station orbits a large near-asteroid, lit by work lamps, scaffolding and pipes visible against the black.
A slow comet traces a faint bright arc at the edge of sensor range, its tail a thin luminous smear.
Magnetic ore concentrations streak the rock face in dark veins, glittering under the rig's floodlights like deep metallic frost.
A salvage tug works a broken rig hulk in the mid-distance, its torch cutting a white spark in the dark.
The belt thins here to scattered lonely rocks far apart, the expanse between them wide and silent and very cold.
A navigation beacon pulses red every few seconds from a distant boulder, its rhythm the only regular thing in the void.
A pressure-cracked asteroid slowly splits along a great fracture, its two halves drifting apart in a cloud of pale debris.
Hard radiation from a solar flare washes across the worksite, instruments flickering, the sun's disc briefly fierce and active.
A survey drone swarm moves through the near belt, hundreds of tiny lights spreading outward like scattered luminous seeds.
The far edge of the belt fades into true interplanetary space, the rock density dropping to nothing, the dark total beyond.
